title: Emergency Fund — Why Every Indian Needs One
text: An emergency fund is money set aside in a liquid (easily accessible) account to cover unexpected expenses — job loss, medical emergency, urgent home or vehicle repair, or family crisis. Financial advisors universally recommend keeping 3–6 months of essential expenses in an emergency fund before investing in stocks, mutual funds, or other instruments. For Indian earners: If your monthly essential expenses (rent, food, bills, EMI) are Rs 15,000, your emergency fund target is Rs 45,000–90,000. Keep it in: (1) A high-interest savings account (some offer 4–7% per year). (2) A liquid mutual fund — redeemable in 1 business day, typically higher returns than savings account. (3) A short-term FD. Do NOT keep it in: stocks, equity mutual funds, cryptocurrency, or any instrument that can lose value quickly. Without an emergency fund, any financial shock forces you into high-interest debt (credit card, personal loan at 15–36% per year). Building an emergency fund of even Rs 20,000–30,000 provides meaningful protection for a first-job earner. Start small and add to it every month before spending on wants.
